data.name: Agricultural Simulator 2011: Extended Edition
data.detailed_description:
In a charming mountain area, you take the role of a classic farmer with all the necessary tasks like cattle breeding, growing grain and other resources, and dealing with products from your farm. Your fields can be cultivated with machines from CLAAS and even your animals have to be taken care of.
The complete Agricultural Simulator allows you to ride many genuine CLAAS tractors. Choose between many different models of tractors, combines, extensions and hangers. Sell your products and invest in better equipment. More powerful machines will help you farm bigger areas. As striving farmer, you have to invest carefully to maximize the crop. Don’t kick over the traces or you won’t be able to upgrade your farm and buy more land. Choose the right seed from different types of grains like barley, rye, or wheat or decide to grow canola or corn. The harvest can be used as animal food, new seed as well as product to be sold on the market. Always have an eye on the market prices so you don’t come out with losses after all the work. Get another main pillar and breed cattle: cows, horses, sheep, hen, and geese. You may even have game animals on your farm and sell them profitably as food. If everything works well, the animals will prosper and you can sell their offspring on the market. Take care of proper feeding, daily care of the stables, and your animals well-being. Hire workers to balance your workload and invest in their further education. The career mode in Agricultural Simulator guarantees a lot of fun. Playing cooperative mode allows you to manage your farm either online or offline with your friends.

New features in the Extended Edition:

  • Optimized and faster engine for higher performance
  • Vehicle models, physics and movement have been reworked and improved
  • New visual effects and graphic options
  • Configurable day and night sky
  • Improved 3D map
  • More streets, a gas station and a new village have been added
  • New places to sell your products
  • Multiplayer mode now has chat
  • Support for Joysticks and Gamepads
  • Improved AI traffic
  • New helper system
  • Fully configurable keyboard control

reviews.review:
Agricultural Simulator 2011: Extended Edition is a farming simulation game developed by Actalogic and published by Libredia that attempts to recreate the challenges and rewards of agricultural life through detailed farm management systems and machinery-focused gameplay. Released during an earlier era of farming simulators, the title approaches the genre with an emphasis on realism and long-term planning rather than fast-paced entertainment. It presents players with the opportunity to build a farming business from modest beginnings while managing crops, livestock, finances, and equipment across a rural environment designed to reflect the responsibilities of operating a working farm.

The game places players inside a mountainous agricultural region where every major aspect of farm ownership falls under their control. Rather than simplifying farming into a sequence of repetitive objectives, Agricultural Simulator 2011 asks players to think strategically about expansion, investment decisions, and productivity. Success requires balancing expenses against profits while gradually improving infrastructure and increasing operational efficiency. The experience leans heavily toward simulation, rewarding patience and planning more than quick reflexes or constant action.

Crop production forms the backbone of progression. Players cultivate multiple agricultural products while learning to manage planting schedules, harvesting cycles, and resource allocation. Building a successful operation requires understanding how individual decisions influence profitability over time. Expanding too aggressively can create financial strain, while careful growth creates opportunities to improve productivity and establish a more stable farming business. The game consistently reinforces the idea that farming involves business management just as much as field work.

Machinery plays an important role throughout the experience. Agricultural Simulator 2011 includes officially licensed farming equipment that allows players to operate tractors, harvesters, and specialized agricultural vehicles inspired by real-world machinery. Purchasing better equipment becomes one of the primary long-term goals because stronger machinery directly improves efficiency and opens opportunities for larger operations. Watching a small farm slowly evolve into a more capable enterprise creates much of the game's sense of progression.

Animal management adds additional depth beyond crop production. Players care for livestock while balancing feeding responsibilities and maintenance requirements alongside broader farm duties. Cows, sheep, horses, poultry, and other animals contribute additional income opportunities while also increasing workload. This extra layer of management helps farming feel more complete by capturing the broader responsibilities associated with agricultural operations rather than limiting gameplay exclusively to crop production.

Economic systems contribute heavily to the simulation aspect. Financial decisions carry meaningful consequences throughout progression. Players must consider investment priorities carefully while balancing short-term profits against long-term expansion goals. Managing resources effectively becomes just as important as operating machinery properly. The business side of farming receives substantial attention, reinforcing the game's attempt to capture agricultural life more authentically.

The Extended Edition introduces adjustments and additions designed to improve the original experience. Improvements to functionality, expanded features, environmental additions, and multiplayer support strengthen the overall package. Cooperative play particularly benefits the experience by allowing players to work together managing farm operations. Farming naturally lends itself well to collaboration, and shared responsibilities help reduce some of the repetitive aspects that can emerge during longer sessions.

The pacing reflects the slower nature of simulation-focused design. Agricultural Simulator 2011 does not attempt to overwhelm players with constant objectives or nonstop progression rewards. Instead, advancement happens gradually. Fields require preparation, harvests take time, and expansion unfolds steadily rather than instantly. Players looking for a slower, methodical experience may appreciate that structure, while others accustomed to faster management games could find the pace demanding.

Visually, the game clearly reflects its generation. Environmental detail and character presentation show their age compared to more modern farming simulators that later refined the formula significantly. Vehicle movement and physics systems occasionally reveal technical roughness, and visual limitations become noticeable during longer sessions. Players approaching the game today should expect older design sensibilities rather than contemporary simulation polish.

Technical imperfections also remain part of the experience. Certain mechanics occasionally lack refinement, and some systems feel less polished than genre leaders that arrived later. Interface elements and handling can sometimes feel awkward by modern standards. These shortcomings do not completely undermine enjoyment, but they create moments where the game's ambition occasionally exceeds its technical execution.

Despite those limitations, Agricultural Simulator 2011: Extended Edition deserves credit for attempting to deliver a broad farming simulation experience during an earlier stage of the genre's development. It embraces agricultural management seriously and provides systems that reward patience and thoughtful planning. The focus remains firmly on creating the feeling of operating a growing agricultural business rather than simply presenting farming as a collection of isolated activities.

For players interested in farming simulations from an earlier generation, Agricultural Simulator 2011 offers an opportunity to experience a title that helped establish ideas later refined by larger productions. Its mechanics may feel dated, and technical issues occasionally surface, but beneath those limitations exists a game built around genuine appreciation for agricultural simulation and long-term farm management.

Agricultural Simulator 2011: Extended Edition shows its age in several areas, but its commitment to detailed farm operations and meaningful progression still provides value for players interested in slower-paced agricultural management experiences.

Rating: 6/10
